title: Getting Started with pmgen: DVT Prediction Model Example
text: pmgen_*() functions implement general simulation-based framework determining sample sizes developing clinical prediction models (CPMs) described Riley et al. (2026). Unlike closed-form criteria pmsampsize(), generalised approach works supervised learning method provides rich summaries model performance degrades different sample sizes. vignette walks complete sample size calculation binary outcome CPM using DVT (deep vein thrombosis) dataset. workflow four steps: Specify reference model: calibrate logistic model target prevalence c-statistic using joint predictor distribution data. Generate target population: create large evaluation dataset reference model. Run simulation: repeatedly sample development datasets varying sizes, fit model, evaluate performance target population. Summarise plot: identify minimum sample size meeting criteria visualise performance changes N.

title: Getting Started with pmgen: DVT Prediction Model Example
text: want develop logistic regression model predict DVT diagnosis 11 binary clinical predictors. dataset (dvt_data) contains 9,805 patients seven studies DVT prevalence approximately 21%. logistic regression model data achieves AUC (c-statistic) 0.79. use observed values specify reference model, hypothetical “true” model representing best achievable performance given predictor set, ask: sample size newly developed model closely approximate reference?
code: library(pmsampsize)  data(dvt_data)  predictors <- c("male", "OCuse", "malignancy", "surgery", "ab_leg_trauma",                  "vein_distension", "calf_diff", "ab_ddimer",                  "pregnancy", "immobile", "clotting")  cat("Rows:", nrow(dvt_data), "\n") #> Rows: 9805 cat("DVT prevalence:", round(mean(dvt_data$dvt), 3), "\n") #> DVT prevalence: 0.209

title: Getting Started with pmgen: DVT Prediction Model Example
text: pmgen_reference() calibrates logistic model target prevalence c-statistic. supply dvt_data joint_data; represents joint distribution predictors target population, used bisection calibration. assume equal relative log-odds weights 11 predictors (coef = NULL), simple default prior knowledge individual predictor effects. relative sizes effects known, supply coef: equal-weights model can give somewhat different results. ref object contains calibrated intercept scaled coefficients achieved prevalence c-statistic.

title: Specify a Reference Model for Sample Size Calculations — pmgen_reference
text: Supplying dataset (joint_data data frame): data frame used directly super-population bisection computing unit information matrix. recommended approach synthetic real pilot data available. Supplying distributional assumptions (joint_data named list): list element specifies marginal distribution one predictor: list(dist = "normal", mean = 50, sd = 10) list(dist = "bernoulli", prob = 0.3). Predictors assumed independent. synthetic population n_synth rows generated bisection. bisection procedure follows Austin's two-step approach: Inner bisection (intercept): fixed scalar s, find intercept b0 mean(plogis(b0 + s * X %*% coef)) = prevalence. Outer bisection (scalar): find s c-statistic resulting model super-population equals cstatistic. Bypassing bisection (bisection = FALSE): supply intercept coef directly final reference model. useful reference model's coefficients already known (e.g. published literature) bisecting synthetic population derived joint_data undesirable — instance, assume predictor independence joint_data data frame (see .fit_marginals()). unit information matrix still computed joint_data usual. Correlation-preserving bisection (bisection_method = "mvn"): joint_data data frame correlated predictors, calibrating synthetic population assumes independence (default "independent" method) can distort calibrated reference model. "mvn" method instead estimates multivariate normal approximation joint_data (means, SDs, full correlation matrix, via cor()) analytically solves linear predictor's mean variance needed hit target prevalence/cstatistic (assuming normal linear predictor), rescales coef resulting predictor combination variance. Binary (0/1) columns generated normal dichotomized match empirical proportion; mildly attenuates correlation predictors relative input correlation matrix (correction applied ). Note bisection without coef gives every predictor coefficient. predictors' true effects differ (size sign), equal-weights model can give noticeably different simulation results (e.g. different expected calibration slope small N) true model; supply coef (relative weights) known.

Based on previous # evidence, the outcome prevalence is anticipated to be 0.018 (1.8%) and the # reported c-statistic was 0.8.  The LP distribution was published and # appeared normally distributed with mean(SD) of -5(2.5).  We target default # CI widths for all but O/E CI width=1 (see Riley et al. for details). We can # use the graph option to check the simulated distribution is appropriate.  pmvalsampsize(type = "b", prevalence = 0.018, cstatistic = 0.8, lpnorm = c(-5,2.5), oeciwidth = 1, simobs = 1000) #> Normal LP distribution with parameters - mean=-5, sd=2.5 #>                          Samp_size Perf    SE CI width #> Criteria 1 - O/E               905  1.0 0.246      1.0 #> Criteria 2 - C-slope          4501  1.0 0.051      0.2 #> Criteria 3 - C statistic      4252  0.8 0.026      0.1 #> Final SS                      4501  1.0 0.051      0.2 #>   #>  Minimum sample size required for model validation based on user inputs = 4501,  #>  with 82 events (assuming an outcome prevalence = 0.018)  #>   #>     # Alternatively, lets assume that the authors provided a distribution of # predicted probabilities (e.g. as part of a calibration plot).  We can use # this to specify parameters for a beta distribution to simulate the LP # distribution as below: pmvalsampsize(type = "b", prevalence = 0.018, cstatistic = 0.8, lpbeta = c(0.5,0.5), oeciwidth = 1, simobs = 1000) #> Beta P distribution with parameters - alpha=0.5, beta=0.5 #>                          Samp_size Perf    SE CI width #> Criteria 1 - O/E               905  1.0 0.246      1.0 #> Criteria 2 - C-slope          1641  1.0 0.051      0.2 #> Criteria 3 - C statistic      4252  0.8 0.026      0.1 #> Final SS                      4252  0.8 0.026      0.1 #>   #>  Minimum sample size required for model validation based on user inputs = 4252,  #>  with 77 events (assuming an outcome prevalence = 0.018)  #>   #>    # Finally, we can use the anticipated c-statistic to simulate the event and # non-event distributions assuming normality and common variances. title: pmsampsize v2.0.0
text: pmsampsize now covers development external validation clinical prediction models, three families functions: pmsampsize() (development), pmvalsampsize() (external validation) new pmgen_*() functions (generalised, simulation-based approach). Existing pmsampsize() calls unchanged (arguments results). Existing pmvalsampsize() calls give results pmvalsampsize 0.1.0, apart lpcstat option type simulated_data_cstat (see ). New package title (“Sample Size Calculations Clinical Prediction Models”), package help page (?pmsampsize-package) CITATION file: citation("pmsampsize") lists package methods papers function. References help pages updated full details DOIs. pmvalsampsize() (sample size external validation prediction model; previously standalone pmvalsampsize package, v0.1.0, released 2023-11-14) now part pmsampsize. Existing pmvalsampsize() calls give results. pmvalsampsize() longer depends pROC. c-statistic simulated data lpcstat option now computed internally (value), simulated_data_cstat returned object now plain number rather pROC auc object. pmvalsampsize() lpcstat option rewritten. mean non-events LP distribution now calculated exactly prevalence cstatistic, instead iterative simulation search user-supplied start value. fixes cases search never finished (e.g. prevalence = 0.2, cstatistic = 0.75). Results lpcstat change slightly mean now precise (e.g. help-file example: criteria 2 sample size 16,175 -> 16,270). lpcstat now logical (lpcstat = TRUE selects option; default FALSE) requires cstatistic greater 0.5. numeric value, used 0.1.0, still accepted treated TRUE, warning. pmvalsampsize() arguments tolerance, increment trace retired (controlled old lpcstat search). ignored, warning, supplied, removed future major version. lpcstat iteration messages replaced single message giving calculated non-events mean simulated vs target prevalence. pmgen_reference() specifies reference model, calibrated target prevalence c-statistic, data distributional assumptions. pmgen_target_population() generates target population developed models evaluated. pmgen_simulate() simulates development datasets candidate sample size, fits model (built : logistic, ridge, lasso, elastic net, Firth; user-supplied fitting function) evaluates performance (c-statistic, calibration slope intercept, O:E ratio, MAPE, RMSPE, Brier score, net benefit, ERVSI). pmgen_min_n() gives smallest sample size meeting user-specified criteria; pmgen_compare() compares two sets results. summary(), print() plot() methods results. Reproducible seed: N value’s simulations use seeds depend seed, N value n_sims. Results therefore identical sequentially parallel (future plan, number workers, using session’s RNGkind() workers ), N value gives results whatever values N, increasing n_sims keeps earlier simulations. dvt_data: example dataset (simulated DVT data, 9,805 patients, 11 binary predictors). New dependencies: MASS, mvtnorm rlang (Imports). Packages needed particular features suggested, required: glmnet (ridge, lasso, elastic net), logistf (Firth), ggplot2 scales (plots), furrr future (parallel simulation). Results without furrr. pmsampsize now requires R >= 4.0.0.
